government.note: Parliamentary republic. The President is directly elected for seven years and is largely ceremonial. The Taoiseach is nominated by Dáil Éireann and appointed by the President. On 1 January 2000 Bertie Ahern led a Fianna Fáil-Progressive Democrats minority coalition formed after the 1997 election.

holders.note: Returned unopposed in 2004 for a second term.

offices.note: Wikidata ends each term on 10 November and starts the next on 11 November; the handover date 11 November is used here. A Presidential Commission acts during a vacancy or absence; no vacancy occurred in this period.

holders.note: FF-PD coalition 1997-2007; FF-Green-PD coalition from June 2007.
FG-Labour coalition 2011-2016; FG-led minority government with independents from May 2016.
FF-FG-Green coalition with a rotating Taoiseach.
FF-FG coalition supported by independents after the 2024 election.

system.note: Single transferable vote in multi-member constituencies (3-5 seats). The outgoing Ceann Comhairle is returned automatically. The Dáil had 166 seats until 2016, 158 in 2016, 160 in 2020 and 174 from 2024. seats_2000 is the 1997 result adjusted for changes up to 1 January 2000 listed in the 28th Dáil article: Democratic Left's 4 TDs joined Labour in January 1999; by-elections in 1998-1999 moved one Fianna Fáil seat to Labour; Séamus Pattison (Labour) sat as Ceann Comhairle; 'others' is Harry Blaney (Independent Fianna Fáil).

43 senators are elected by STV on five vocational panels by an electorate of TDs, outgoing senators and local councillors; 6 are elected by graduates of two university constituencies; 11 are nominated by the Taoiseach. seats_2000 is the 21st Seanad (first met 17 September 1997: FF 29, FG 16, Labour 4, PD 4, independents 7) adjusted for changes to 1 January 2000: one Labour seat lost to the Dáil and won by FF at a 1998 by-election; Brendan Ryan (independent) joined Labour in January 1999; the death of Patrick McGowan (FF) and the resignation of Pat Gallagher (Labour) in October 1999 left two seats vacant until the June 2000 by-elections.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from 1997 Dáil first-preference shares: Fianna Fáil 39.3% (christian_democrat), Fine Gael 27.9% (liberal_conservative), Labour 10.4% plus Democratic Left 2.5% (merged into Labour in January 1999; social_democrat), Progressive Democrats 4.7% (classical_liberal), Greens 2.8%, Sinn Féin 2.5% plus Socialist Party 0.7% (democratic_socialist), and independents and minor parties about 9.2% (big_tent). The minority government relied on several independent TDs.
